title.zh: 卷五十六 列傳第三十七 倖臣
title.raw: 卷五十六 列傳第三十七 倖臣 Volume 56 Biographies 37: Trusted Officials

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第五十六 列傳第三十七

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biographies 37
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biography 37

sentences.zh: 紀僧真 劉係宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 呂文度

translations.literal: Ji Sengzhen; Liu Zongzong; Ru Faliang; Lü Wenxian; Lü Wendu
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sengzhen; Liu Zongzong; Ru Faliang; Lü Wenxian; and Lü Wendu

sentences.zh: 有天象，必有人事焉。

translations.literal: When there are celestial phenomena, there must be human affairs corresponding to them.
translations.idiomatic: When signs appear in the heavens, corresponding events unfold among men.

sentences.zh: 倖臣一星，列于帝座。

translations.literal: The Favored-Officials star is arrayed beside the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The star of favored officials stands ranked beside the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 經禮立教，亦著近臣之服。

translations.literal: The canonical rites that establish teaching also prescribe vestments for intimate ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The classical rites that ground moral instruction likewise set down garb for those who serve close at hand.

sentences.zh: 親倖之義，其來已久。

translations.literal: The meaning of personal favor has a history stretching far back.
translations.idiomatic: The institution of intimate favor at court reaches deep into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 爰自衰周，侯伯專命，桓、文霸主，至于戰國，寵用近習，不乏於時矣。

translations.literal: From the declining Zhou onward, feudal lords held sole command; Duke Huan and Duke Wen were hegemons; down through the Warring States, imperial favorites drawn from close attendants were never lacking for long.
translations.idiomatic: From late Zhou, when regional lords held unchecked authority, through Duke Huan and Duke Wen as hegemons and on into the Warring States, rulers who pampered men at their side were never absent from the age.

sentences.zh: 漢文幸鄧通，雖錢徧天下，位止郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; though his wealth spread across the realm, his rank stopped at Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; though his coin filled the realm, his office rose no higher than Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 孝武韓嫣、霍去病，遂至侍中大司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu with Han Yan and Huo Qubing raised them to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, Han Yan and Huo Qubing rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 迄于魏、晉，世任權重，才位稍爽，而信倖唯均。

translations.literal: By Wei and Jin, the age entrusted great power to them; talent and office slipped somewhat apart, yet trust in favorites alone kept pace.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wei and Jin the times gave them heavy authority; talent and rank grew slightly mismatched, yet reliance on favorites alone held steady.

sentences.zh: 中書之職，舊掌機務。

translations.literal: The post of Palace Secretary had of old held charge of confidential state business.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had long held charge of confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢元以令僕用事，魏明以監令專權，及在中朝，猶爲重寄。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han put the Director and Deputy Director in control; Emperor Ming of Wei let the Supervisor and Director monopolize power; even at the central court they remained a weighty commission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han had the Director and Deputy Director run affairs; Emperor Ming of Wei had the Supervisor and Director monopolize authority; even at the central court they remained a weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 陳准歸任上司，荀勗恨於失職。

translations.literal: Chen Huai surrendered authority to his superiors; Xun Xu resented his loss of office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huai yielded his post to his superiors; Xun Xu nursed resentment at losing his office.

sentences.zh: 晉令舍人位居九品，江左置通事郎，管司詔誥。

translations.literal: In Jin the Orderly Clerk ranked in the nine grades; east of the Yangtze they established the Communicator Gentleman to manage imperial decrees and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin the Secretariat clerk held ninth-rank standing; east of the Yangtze they set up the Communicator Gentleman to oversee edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 其後郎還爲侍郎，而舍人亦稱通事。

translations.literal: Later the Gentleman returned to being Deputy Director, while the clerk was also called Communicator.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Gentleman post reverted to Deputy Director, while the clerk was also styled Communicator.

sentences.zh: 元帝用琅邪劉超，以謹慎居職。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye for his careful conduct in office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Jin used Liu Chao of Langye, who served with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 宋文世，秋當、周糾竝出寒門。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both came from humble households.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both came from humble households.

sentences.zh: 孝武以來，士庶雜選，如東海鮑照，以才學知名。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu onward, gentry and commoners were mixed in selection; such as Bao Zhao of Donghai, renowned for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaowu onward, noble and common birth were mixed in selection; such as Bao Zhao of Donghai, famed for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 又用魯郡巢尚之，江夏王義恭以爲非選。

translations.literal: They also used Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery; the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, held this not proper selection.
translations.idiomatic: They also employed Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery; the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, deemed this an improper choice.

sentences.zh: 帝遣尚書二十餘牒，宣敕論辯，義恭乃歎曰：「人主誠知人。

translations.literal: The emperor sent more than twenty memorials from the Secretariat to proclaim edicts and debate; Yigong sighed and said: "The sovereign truly knows men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent more than twenty Secretariat documents to proclaim edicts and argue the point; Yigong sighed and said, "The ruler truly knows men."

sentences.zh: 」及明帝世，胡母顥、阮佃夫之徒，專爲佞倖矣。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Ming, Hu Mugao, Ruan Tianfu and their sort were devoted flatterers alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Ming, Hu Mugao, Ruan Tianfu, and their like were flatterers and favorites through and through.

sentences.zh: 齊初亦用久勞，及以親信。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi they also employed men of long service and their personal intimates.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Qi they likewise used men of long service and personal intimates.

sentences.zh: 關讞表啓，發署詔敕。

translations.literal: They controlled memorials and reports, issued and endorsed edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: They controlled memorials and reports and issued and countersigned edicts and commands.

sentences.zh: 頗涉辭翰者，亦爲詔文，侍郎之局，復見侵矣。

translations.literal: Those somewhat versed in letters also drafted edicts; the jurisdiction of the Deputy Director was encroached upon again.
translations.idiomatic: Those with some skill in letters also drafted edicts; the Deputy Director's domain was encroached upon once more.

sentences.zh: 建武世，詔命殆不關中書，專出舍人。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era, edicts and orders hardly passed through the Secretariat; they issued solely from the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era, edicts and commands scarcely touched the Secretariat and issued solely from the clerks.

sentences.zh: 省內舍人四人，所直四省，其下有主書令史，舊用武官，宋改文吏，人數無員。

translations.literal: Within the Secretariat four clerks, each supervising one of the four bureaus; beneath them were chief clerks and registrars; originally military officers were used, the Song changed them to civil clerks, with no fixed headcount.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the Secretariat were four clerks, each in charge of one of the four bureaus; below them were chief clerks and registrars; formerly military officers were used, but the Song changed them to civil clerks, with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 莫非左右要密，天下文簿板籍，入副其省，萬機嚴祕，有如尚書外司。

translations.literal: All were indispensable intimate attendants at the ruler's side; the realm's documents and registers entered their duplicate files, state affairs closely guarded like an outer Secretariat ministry.
translations.idiomatic: All were indispensable intimates at the ruler's side; the realm's documents and registers were copied into their offices, and state secrets were guarded as closely as in an outer arm of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 領武官，有制局監，領器仗兵役，亦用寒人被恩幸者。

translations.literal: To lead military officers there was the Bureau of Arms Supervisor, commanding weapons and troops; they too employed men of humble birth who had received imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: For military affairs there was the Bureau of Arms Supervisor, commanding weapons and troops; they too used men of humble birth who had won imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 今立《倖臣篇》，以繼前史之末云。

translations.literal: Now this "Favored Officials" chapter is set down to follow the end of earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: This "Favored Officials" chapter is now set down to continue where earlier histories leave off.

sentences.zh: 紀僧真，丹陽建康人也。

translations.literal: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jianye in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jianye in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 僧真少隨逐征西將軍蕭思話及子惠開，皆被賞遇。

translations.literal: As a youth Sengzhen followed the western campaign general Xiao Sihua and his son Huikai, and at each step was rewarded with favor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Sengzhen followed the western campaign general Xiao Sihua and his son Huikai, and at every turn was shown favor.

sentences.zh: 惠開性苛，僧真以微過見罰，旣而委任如舊。

translations.literal: Huikai was harsh by nature; Sengzhen was punished for a minor fault, yet afterward was entrusted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was harsh by nature; Sengzhen was punished for a minor offense, yet afterward was entrusted as before.

sentences.zh: 及罷益州還都，不得志，僧真事之愈謹。

translations.literal: When Huikai left Yizhou and returned to the capital, discontented with his lot, Sengzhen served him all the more devotedly.
translations.idiomatic: When Huikai left Yizhou and returned to the capital, frustrated in his ambitions, Sengzhen served him with still greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 惠開臨終歎曰：「紀僧真方當富貴，我不見也。

translations.literal: At the end Huikai sighed: "Ji Sengzhen is about to grow rich and noble - I shall not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his life Huikai sighed: "Ji Sengzhen is about to grow rich and noble—I shall not live to see it."

sentences.zh: 」乃以僧真託劉秉、周顒。

translations.literal: He thereupon entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.
translations.idiomatic: With that he entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，惠開在益州，土反，被圍危急，有道人謂之曰：「城圍尋解。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huikai was in Yizhou, the native tribes rebelled and he was besieged in critical peril; a Daoist told him: "The siege will soon be lifted."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huikai was in Yizhou, the native tribes rebelled and he was besieged in dire peril; a Daoist told him, "The siege will soon be lifted."

sentences.zh: 檀越貴門後方大興，無憂外賊也。

translations.literal: "Patron, your noble house will flourish hereafter; have no fear of outside enemies."
translations.idiomatic: "Patron, your noble house will flourish hereafter—have no fear of outside enemies."

sentences.zh: 」惠開密謂僧真曰：「我子弟見在者，竝無異才。

translations.literal: Huikai secretly told Sengzhen: "My sons and younger brothers now living are without unusual talent."
translations.idiomatic: Huikai secretly told Sengzhen, "My sons and younger brothers now living all lack unusual talent."

sentences.zh: 政是道成耳。

translations.literal: "It is only Daocheng."
translations.idiomatic: "None but Daocheng."

sentences.zh: 」僧真憶其言，乃請事太祖。

translations.literal: Sengzhen remembered his words and thereupon asked to enter the service of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen remembered his words and thereupon asked to enter Emperor Gao's service.

sentences.zh: 隨從在淮陰，以閑書題，令荅遠近書疏。

translations.literal: Following the campaign at Huaiyin, because he was skilled at casual brushwork he was ordered to answer letters from near and far.
translations.idiomatic: While following the army at Huaiyin, because he was skilled at informal brushwork he was ordered to answer letters from near and far.

sentences.zh: 自寒官歷至太祖冠軍府參軍、主簿。

translations.literal: From a humble post he advanced through service to staff officer and chief clerk in Emperor Gao's Champion-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: From a humble post he rose through service to staff officer and chief clerk in Emperor Gao's Champion-general's office.

sentences.zh: 僧真夢蒿艾生滿江，驚而白之。

translations.literal: Sengzhen dreamed that mugwort and artemisia filled the river; alarmed, he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen dreamed mugwort and artemisia filled the river; alarmed, he reported the dream.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「詩人採蕭，蕭卽艾也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said: "The poets gather mugwort - 'mugwort' is also ai [homophone for surname Xiao/Ai]."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "The poets gather mugwort—'mugwort' is also ai."

sentences.zh: 蕭生斷流，卿勿廣言。

translations.literal: "'Ai grows across the broken stream' - do not speak broadly of this."
translations.idiomatic: "'Ai grows across the broken stream'—do not speak broadly of this."

sentences.zh: 」其見親如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree of his intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how close he was to him.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，從太祖頓新亭，拒桂陽賊。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yuanhui era he followed Emperor Gao to camp at Xinting to resist the rebels of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhui era he followed Emperor Gao to camp at Xinting and resist the Guiyang rebels.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠朗突入東門，僧真與左右共拒戰。

translations.literal: Xiao Huilang burst through the eastern gate; Sengzhen with the guards fought them off together.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huilang burst through the eastern gate; Sengzhen and the guards fought them off together.

sentences.zh: 賊退，太祖命僧真領親兵，遊邏城中。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated, Emperor Gao ordered Sengzhen to lead the personal guard patrolling inside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels retreated, Emperor Gao ordered Sengzhen to lead the personal guard on patrol within the walls.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除南臺御史、太祖領軍功曹。

translations.literal: When affairs settled he was appointed Censor of the Southern Bureau and merit officer on Emperor Gao's General-in-Chief staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed he was appointed Censor of the Southern Bureau and merit officer on Emperor Gao's General-in-Chief staff.

sentences.zh: 上將廢立，謀之袁粲、褚淵，僧真啓上曰：「今朝廷猖狂，人不自保，天下之望，不在袁、褚。

translations.literal: When the Prince was about to depose and enthrone, consulting Yuan Can and Chu Yuan, Sengzhen memorialized: "Today the court is reckless and men cannot protect themselves; the hope of the realm does not rest on Yuan and Chu."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was about to depose and enthrone, consulting Yuan Can and Chu Yuan, Sengzhen memorialized: "Today the court is reckless and men cannot protect themselves; the hope of the realm does not rest on Yuan and Chu."

sentences.zh: 明公豈得默己，坐受夷滅。

translations.literal: "My lord, how can you keep silent and sit by while you are destroyed root and branch?"
translations.idiomatic: "How can you, my lord, keep silent and sit by while you are destroyed root and branch?"

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，仰希熟慮。

translations.literal: "The moment of survival or extinction - I beg you to ponder it deeply."
translations.idiomatic: "The moment of survival or extinction—I beg you to ponder it deeply."

sentences.zh: 」太祖納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲度廣陵起兵，僧真又啓曰：「主上雖復狂釁，虐加萬民，而累世皇基，猶固盤石。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao wished to cross to Guangling and raise troops; Sengzhen again memorialized: "Although the sovereign is still reckless and cruel beyond the myriad people, generations of imperial foundation remain firm as bedrock."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao planned to cross to Guangling and raise troops; Sengzhen again urged: "Though the sovereign is still reckless and cruel to the myriad people, generations of imperial foundation remain firm as bedrock."

sentences.zh: 今百口北度，何必得俱。

translations.literal: "Now a hundred mouths cross north - must all go together?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now a hundred mouths cross north—must all go together?"

sentences.zh: 縱得廣陵城，天子居深宮施號令，目明公爲逆，何以避此？

translations.literal: "Even if you take Guangling city, the Son of Heaven sits deep in the palace issuing commands and marks you as rebel - how escape that?"
translations.idiomatic: "Even if you take Guangling city, the Son of Heaven sits deep in the palace issuing commands and marks you as rebel—how would you escape that?"

sentences.zh: 如其不勝，則應北走胡中，竊謂此非萬全策也。

translations.literal: "If you do not prevail, you must flee north among the barbarians - I venture this is not a plan without flaw."
translations.idiomatic: "If you do not prevail, you must flee north among the barbarians—I venture this is not a plan without flaw."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿顧家，豈能逐我行耶。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "You think of your family - could you really follow me in going?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "You think of your family—could you really follow me in going?"

sentences.zh: 」僧真頓首稱無貳。

translations.literal: Sengzhen kowtowed and said he would not be of two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen kowtowed and declared he would not be of two minds.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，除員外郎，帶東武城令。

translations.literal: First year of Shengming, appointed Outer Gentleman with concurrent magistrate of Dongwucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed Outer Gentleman with concurrent magistrate of Dongwucheng.

sentences.zh: 尋除給事中、邵陵王參軍。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Giver of Counsel and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Giver of Counsel and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 太祖坐東府高樓，望石頭城，僧真在側。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao sat in the high tower of the Eastern Residence looking toward Stone Fortress city; Sengzhen was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao sat in the high tower of the Eastern Residence looking toward Stone Fortress city, with Sengzhen at his side.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諸將勸我誅袁、劉，我意不欲便爾。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "The generals urge me to kill Yuan and Liu; I am not yet willing to do so immediately."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "The generals urge me to kill Yuan and Liu; I am not yet willing to do so immediately."

sentences.zh: 」及沈攸之事起，從太祖入朝堂。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair erupted he followed Emperor Gao into the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled he followed Emperor Gao into the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 石頭反夜，太祖遣衆軍掩討。

translations.literal: On the night of the Stone Fortress revolt Emperor Gao sent the host of armies to take it by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Stone Fortress rose in revolt, Emperor Gao sent the armies to take it by surprise.

sentences.zh: 宮城中望石頭火光及呌聲甚盛，人懷不測。

translations.literal: In the palace they saw fire and cries from Stone Fortress very loud; men were filled with uncertainty.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace they saw fire and cries from Stone Fortress very loud; everyone was filled with uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 僧真謂衆曰：「呌聲不絕，是必官軍所攻。

translations.literal: Sengzhen told the crowd: "The cries do not cease - that must be the government troops attacking."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told the crowd, "The cries do not cease—that must be the government troops attacking."

sentences.zh: 火光起者，賊不容自燒其城，此必官軍勝也。

translations.literal: "Where fire rises, the rebels would not burn their own city - the government troops must have won."
translations.idiomatic: "Where fire rises, the rebels would not burn their own city—the government troops must have won."

sentences.zh: 」尋而啓石頭平。

translations.literal: Before long came word that Stone Fortress was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Stone Fortress had been pacified.

sentences.zh: 上出頓新亭，使僧真領千人在帳內。

translations.literal: The Prince went out to camp at Xinting and ordered Sengzhen to command a thousand men inside the tents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao went out to camp at Xinting and ordered Sengzhen to command a thousand men inside the tents.

sentences.zh: 初，上在領軍府，令僧真學上手迹下名，至是報荅書疏，皆付僧真，上觀之，笑曰：「我亦不復能別也。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the General-in-Chief's office the Prince had Sengzhen learn his hand in signing at the bottom; now replies to letters were all entrusted to Sengzhen; the Prince looked and laughed: "I could not tell the difference myself anymore."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the General-in-Chief's office Emperor Gao had Sengzhen learn his hand in signing at the bottom; now replies to letters were all entrusted to Sengzhen; the Prince looked and laughed, "I could not tell the difference myself anymore."

sentences.zh: 」初，上在淮陰治城，得一錫趺，大數尺，下有篆文，莫能識者。

translations.literal: Earlier, while fortifying the city at Huaiyin he obtained a bronze pedestal base several feet across, with seal script beneath that no one could read.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while building the city at Huaiyin, he found a bronze pedestal several feet across with seal script below that no one could read.

sentences.zh: 僧真曰：「何須辨此文字，此自久遠之物，九錫之徵也。

translations.literal: Sengzhen said: "Why bother to decipher these characters? This is a thing of great antiquity - a sign of the Nine Bestowals."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen said, "Why bother to decipher these characters? This is a thing of great antiquity—a sign of the Nine Bestowals."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿勿妄言。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said: "Do not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "Do not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 」及上將拜齊公，已剋日，有楊袓之謀於臨軒作難。

translations.literal: When the Prince was about to receive title as Duke of Qi, the day was already set, and Yang Zuzhi plotted to make trouble at the audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was about to receive title as Duke of Qi, the day was already set, and Yang Zuzhi plotted to make trouble at the audience.

sentences.zh: 僧真更請上選吉辰，尋而祖之事覺。

translations.literal: Sengzhen again asked the Prince to choose an auspicious day; soon Zuzhi's plot was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen again asked Emperor Gao to choose an auspicious day; soon Zuzhi's plot was exposed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「無卿言，亦當致小狼狽，此亦何異呼遝之冰。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Without your words we would still have met a small embarrassment - how is this different from Huzi Guang's warning about the ice?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "Without your words we would still have met a small embarrassment—how is this different from Huzi Guang's warning about the ice?"

sentences.zh: 」轉齊國中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Clerk of the State of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Secretariat Clerk of the State of Qi.

sentences.zh: 宋世道人楊法持，與太祖有舊。

translations.literal: During Song the Daoist Yang Fachi had old ties with Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times the Daoist Yang Fachi had long-standing ties with Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，宣傳密謀。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he spread word of secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhui he circulated word of secret plots.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，以爲僧正。

translations.literal: In Shengming he was made chief of monks.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming he was made chief of the Buddhist clergy.

sentences.zh: 建元初，罷道，爲寧朔將軍，封州陵縣男，三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he left orders and became General Pacifying the North, enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling county with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyuan he left the priesthood, became General Pacifying the North, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年，虜圍朐山，遣法持爲軍主，領支軍救援。

translations.literal: In the second year when the barbarians besieged Qushan he sent Fachi as army commander leading a detached force to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the barbarians besieged Qushan, he sent Fachi as army commander leading a detached force to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，坐役使將客，奪其鮭稟，削封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming for employing and robbing guests of their salmon provisions he lost his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming, for employing and robbing guests of their salmon provisions, he lost his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 劉係宗，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zongzong was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzong was a man of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少便書畫，爲宋竟陵王誕子景粹侍書。

translations.literal: As a youth he was skilled at calligraphy and painting; he served as attendant scribe to Jingchun, son of the Prince of Jingling, Liu Dan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was skilled at calligraphy and painting and served as attendant scribe to Jingchun, son of the Prince of Jingling, Liu Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕舉兵廣陵，城內皆死，敕沈慶之赦係宗，以爲東宮侍書。

translations.literal: When Dan raised troops at Guangling everyone in the city was put to death; an edict ordered Shen Qingzhi to pardon Zongzong and appoint him attendant scribe to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan raised troops at Guangling and everyone in the city was executed, an edict had Shen Qingzhi pardon Zongzong and name him attendant scribe to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，爲主書。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he was chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 以寒官累遷至勳品。

translations.literal: From humble office he rose step by step to merit-grade rank.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from humble office step by step, he reached merit-grade rank.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，爲奉朝請，兼中書通事舍人，員外郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhui he was Court Gentleman, concurrent Communicator Clerk of the Secretariat and Outer Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhui he was a Court Gentleman, serving concurrently as Communicator Clerk of the Secretariat and as Outer Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 封始興南亭侯，食邑三百七十戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing with a fief of three hundred seventy households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing with a fief of three hundred seventy households.

sentences.zh: 帶秣陵令。

translations.literal: Concurrent magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He held concurrent office as magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 太祖廢蒼梧，明旦，呼正直舍人虞整，醉不能起，係宗歡喜奉命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao deposed Emperor Cangwu, at dawn he summoned the upright-duty clerk Yu Zheng, who was drunk and could not rise; Zongzong gladly accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao deposed Emperor Cangwu, at dawn he summoned the upright-duty clerk Yu Zheng, who was drunk and could not rise; Zongzong gladly took the command.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「今天地重開，是卿盡力之日。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said: "Heaven and earth are newly opened - this is the day for you to exert yourself to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "Heaven and earth are newly opened—this is the day for you to exert yourself to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 」使寫諸處分敕令，及四方書疏。

translations.literal: He had him write all orders and edicts of assignment and letters to the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He had him draft all orders and edicts of assignment and letters to the four directions.

sentences.zh: 使主書十人書吏二十人配之，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He gave him ten chief clerks and twenty clerks to assist; everything accorded with intent.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him ten chief clerks and twenty clerks to assist; everything met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 除羽林監，轉步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, then transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 仍除龍驤將軍，出爲海鹽令。

translations.literal: He was then made General of Dragon Cavalry and went out as magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made General of Dragon Cavalry and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，除龍驤將軍、建康令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao took the throne, Zongzong was appointed General of Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, he was appointed General of Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，除寧朔將軍，令如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was made General Pacifying the North, his command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he was made General Pacifying the North, with his duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋轉右軍將軍、淮陵太守，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to General of the Right Army and administrator of Huailing, concurrent Communicator Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to General of the Right Army and administrator of Huailing, while retaining his post as Communicator Clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母喪自解，起爲寧朔將軍，復本職。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he resigned; on mourning's end he was restored as General Pacifying the North and resumed his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he resigned; when mourning ended he was restored as General Pacifying the North and resumed his former duties.

sentences.zh: 四年，白賊唐宇之起，宿衞兵東討，遣係宗隨軍慰勞，徧至遭賊郡縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the White Bandit Tang Yuzhi rose; the palace guard marched east to attack; Zongzong was sent with the army to comfort and reward, reaching every commandery and county that had suffered the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the White Bandit Tang Yuzhi rose; the palace guard marched east to suppress him; Zongzong was sent with the army to comfort and reward troops, reaching every commandery and county that had suffered the rebels.

sentences.zh: 百姓被驅逼者，悉無所問，還復民伍。

translations.literal: Commoners who had been driven and pressed were all left unpunished and restored to civilian status.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who had been driven into service were all left unpunished and restored to civilian rolls.

sentences.zh: 係宗還，上曰：「此段有征無戰，以時平蕩，百姓安怗，甚快也。

translations.literal: When Zongzong returned, the emperor said: "This campaign had expeditions without battles; it was pacified in season and the people are settled—very satisfying."
translations.idiomatic: When Zongzong returned, the emperor said, "This campaign had expeditions without battles; it was pacified in good time and the people are settled—very satisfying."

sentences.zh: 」賜係宗錢帛。

translations.literal: He bestowed money and silks on Zongzong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed money and silks on Zongzong.

sentences.zh: 上欲脩治白下城，難於動役。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to repair and fortify the White Fortress city but found mobilizing labor difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to repair the White Fortress walls but found it hard to mobilize labor.

sentences.zh: 係宗啓謫役東民丁隨宇之爲逆者，上從之。

translations.literal: Zongzong memorialized to conscript eastern commoner laborers who had followed Yuzhi in rebellion; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzong memorialized to conscript eastern commoner laborers who had followed Yuzhi in rebellion; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 後車駕講武，上履行白下城，曰：「劉係宗爲國家得此一城。」

translations.literal: Later when the emperor reviewed troops and walked the White Fortress walls, he said: "Liu Zongzong won this city for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Later when the emperor reviewed troops and walked the White Fortress walls, he said, "Liu Zongzong won this city for the state."

sentences.zh: 永明中，虜使書常令係宗題答，祕書書局皆隷之。

translations.literal: In Yongming, barbarian envoys' letters were regularly entrusted to Zongzong for inscription and reply; the Secretariat script offices were all subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, barbarian envoys' letters were regularly entrusted to Zongzong for inscription and reply; the Secretariat script offices were all placed under him.

sentences.zh: 再爲少府，遷游擊將軍、魯郡太守。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of the Privy Purse, then transferred to General Who Patrols and administrator of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed the Privy Purse, then became General Who Patrols and administrator of Lu.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，除驍騎將軍，仍除寧朔將軍、宣城太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Deposed of Lin took the throne he was made General of Valiant Cavalry, then again General Pacifying the North and administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Deposed of Lin ascended, Zongzong was made General of Valiant Cavalry, then again General Pacifying the North and administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 係宗久在朝省，閑於職事。

translations.literal: Zongzong had long served in the central offices and was skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzong had long served in the central offices and knew administrative work well.

sentences.zh: 明帝曰：「學士不堪治國，唯大讀書耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming said: "Scholars cannot govern the state—they only read many books."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming said, "Scholars cannot govern the state—they only read many books."

sentences.zh: 一劉係宗足持如此輩五百人。

translations.literal: One Liu Zongzong is enough to manage five hundred such men.
translations.idiomatic: A single Liu Zongzong is enough to manage five hundred such men.

sentences.zh: 」其重吏事如此。

translations.literal: "" Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，卒官，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋大明世，出身爲小史，歷齋幹扶。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song he began as a petty clerk and passed through posts as orderly and attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song in the Daming era he started as a petty clerk and worked through orderly and attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 孝武末年，作酒法，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he made wine regulations with excessive flogging; on hunts in the lands south of the Yangtze he selected one hundred eighty white-robed attendants, all with wealthy faces and households; going south with him, more than half received the lash.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he made wine regulations with excessive flogging; on hunts in the lands south of the Yangtze he selected one hundred eighty white-robed attendants, all from wealthy households; going south with him, more than half received the lash.

sentences.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啓出家得爲道人。

translations.literal: Faliang was fearful and anxious and seized the occasion to request leaving home and becoming a Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang was fearful and anxious and seized the occasion to request leaving home and becoming a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，用爲兖州刺史孟次陽典籤。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he left orders and attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, who used him as chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he left the priesthood and attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, who used him as chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累至太祖冠軍府行參軍。

translations.literal: He rose step by step to acting staff officer in Emperor Gao's Champion-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed step by step to acting staff officer in Emperor Gao's Champion-general's office.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，除殿中將軍，爲晉熙王郢州典籤，除長兼殿中御史。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhui he was appointed General of the Palace and made chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou; appointed chief concurrent Censor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhui he was appointed General of the Palace and made chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou; he was also appointed chief concurrent Censor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 巴東王子響於荊州殺僚佐，上遣軍西上，使法亮宣旨慰勞，安撫子響。

translations.literal: The Prince of Badong, Zixiang, killed his staff in Jingzhou; the emperor sent armies west and ordered Faliang to proclaim the imperial will to comfort and reassure Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Badong, Zixiang, killed his staff in Jingzhou, the court sent armies west and ordered Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and reassure Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 法亮至江津，子響呼法亮，法亮疑畏不肯往。

translations.literal: Faliang reached Jiangjin; Zixiang summoned Faliang, but Faliang in suspicion and fear would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang reached Jiangjin; Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, would not go.

sentences.zh: 又求見傳詔，法亮又不遣。

translations.literal: Zixiang again asked to see the edict-bearer; Faliang again would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang again asked to see the edict-bearer; Faliang again refused to send him.

sentences.zh: 故子響怒，遣兵破尹略軍。

translations.literal: Therefore Zixiang was enraged and sent troops to defeat Yin Lue's army.
translations.idiomatic: So Zixiang was enraged and sent troops to defeat Yin Lue's army.

sentences.zh: 事平，法亮至江陵，刑賞處分，皆稱敕斷決。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled Faliang reached Jiangling; punishments and rewards were all decided in the name of imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled Faliang reached Jiangling; punishments and rewards were all decided in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 軍還，上悔誅子響，法亮被責。

translations.literal: When the army returned the emperor regretted executing Zixiang; Faliang was blamed.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned the emperor regretted killing Zixiang, and Faliang was blamed.

sentences.zh: 少時，親任如舊。

translations.literal: Before long he was trusted and employed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he enjoyed the same trust as before.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Deposed of Lin took the throne he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Deposed of Lin took power he was named Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，爲前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was made General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing's first year he became General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 延昌殿爲世祖陰室，藏諸御服。

translations.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing all imperial vestments.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, where all imperial vestments were stored.

sentences.zh: 二少帝竝居西殿，高宗卽位住東齋，開陰室出世祖白紗帽防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: The two young emperors both dwelt in the western hall; when Emperor Ming took the throne he lived in the eastern quarters; opening the private chamber they brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and body-guard knife; Faliang sobbed with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The two young emperors both dwelt in the western hall; when Emperor Ming took the throne he lived in the eastern quarters; opening the private chamber they brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and body-guard knife, and Faliang sobbed with tears.

sentences.zh: 除游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Patrols.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Patrols.

sentences.zh: 高武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。

translations.literal: Few of Emperor Gao's old intimates survived; Faliang because he managed documentary affairs was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Few of Emperor Gao's old intimates survived; because Faliang managed documentary affairs he was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained as before.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, when Wang Jingze's affair was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai's first year, once Wang Jingze's revolt was crushed, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort.

sentences.zh: 出法亮爲大司農，中書勢利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受，旣而代人已致，法亮垂涕而出。

translations.literal: Faliang was sent out as Grand Minister of Agriculture; the Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and Faliang was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined and would not accept; yet before long his replacement had arrived, and Faliang left in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang was sent out as Grand Minister of Agriculture; the Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and Faliang was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined, yet before long his replacement had arrived, and Faliang left in tears.

sentences.zh: 年六十四，卒官。

translations.literal: At age sixty-four he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 文顯治事以刻覈被知。

translations.literal: Wenxian was known for handling affairs with harsh scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenxian was known for handling affairs with harsh scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 三年，帶南清河太守。

translations.literal: In the third year he held concurrent office as administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In his third year in office he also served as administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 與茹法亮等迭出入爲舍人，竝見親倖。

translations.literal: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns entering and leaving as clerks, all receiving intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns serving as clerks, all receiving intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 四方餉遺，歲各數百萬，竝造大宅，聚山開池。

translations.literal: Gifts from the four directions came to each in millions every year; all built great mansions, heaped hills and opened pools.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from the four directions came to each in millions every year; all built great mansions, heaped hills, and opened pools.

sentences.zh: 五年，爲建康令，轉長水校尉，歷帶南泰山、南譙太守，尋爲司徒中兵參軍，淮南太守，直舍人省。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was magistrate of Jiankang, transferred to Commandant of the Long River, successively held concurrent posts as administrator of Southern Taishan and Southern Qiao, then staff officer for military affairs to the Minister of State, administrator of Huainan, and duty clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was magistrate of Jiankang, transferred to Commandant of the Long River, and successively held concurrent posts as administrator of Southern Taishan and Southern Qiao, then staff officer for military affairs to the Minister of State, administrator of Huainan, and duty clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷左中郎將，南東莞太守，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He rose step by step to Left Commandant of the Center, administrator of Southern Dongguan, and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Left Commandant of the Center, administrator of Southern Dongguan, and General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，以文顯守少府，見任使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assisted in government, Wenxian was put in charge of the Privy Purse and was trusted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Ming held the regency, Wenxian was placed over the Privy Purse and given real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 歷建武、永元之世，尚書右丞，少府卿。

translations.literal: Through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras he served as Right Director of the Secretariat and Minister of the Privy Purse.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jianwu and Yongyuan he was Right Director of the Secretariat and Minister of the Privy Purse.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 呂文度，會稽人。

translations.literal: Lü Wendu was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wendu came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 宋世爲細作金銀庫吏，竹局匠。

translations.literal: During Song he was clerk in the fine crafts gold and silver treasury and bamboo-works artisan.
translations.idiomatic: During Song he was clerk in the fine crafts gold and silver treasury and a bamboo-works artisan.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，爲射雉典事，隨監莫脩宗上郢。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting, following Supervisor Mo Xiuzong up to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting and followed Supervisor Mo Xiuzong up to Ying.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮盆城拒沈攸之，文度仍留伏事，知軍隊雜役，以此見親。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu garrisoned Pencheng to resist Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained to serve in secret, knowing military miscellaneous duties, and for this was shown favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu garrisoned Pencheng to resist Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained to serve in secret, knowing military miscellaneous duties, and for this won favor.

sentences.zh: 從還都，爲石頭城監，仍度東宮。

translations.literal: Following the return to the capital he was supervisor of Stone Fortress city and also passed through the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he was supervisor of Stone Fortress city and also passed through the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，爲制局監，位至員外郎，帶南濮陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was Bureau of Arms Supervisor, rising to Outer Gentleman with concurrent administrator of Southern Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne he became Bureau of Arms Supervisor, rising to Outer Gentleman with concurrent administrator of Southern Puyang.

sentences.zh: 殿內軍隊及發遣外鎮人，悉關之，甚有要勢。

translations.literal: Palace troops and men dispatched to outer garrisons all passed through him; he held very great influence.
translations.idiomatic: Palace troops and men dispatched to outer garrisons all passed through him, and he held very great influence.

sentences.zh: 故世傳越州嘗缺，上覔一直事人往越州，文度啓其所知費延宗合旨，上卽以爲刺史。

translations.literal: Hence it was said in the world that Yuezhou was once vacant; the emperor sought a straight-duty man to go to Yuezhou; Wendu memorialized that Fei Yanzong, whom he knew, suited intent, and the emperor immediately made him inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it was said that Yuezhou was once vacant; the emperor sought a straight-duty man to go to Yuezhou; Wendu memorialized that Fei Yanzong, whom he knew, suited intent, and the emperor immediately made him inspector.

sentences.zh: 永明中，敕親近不得輙有申薦，人士免官，寒人鞭一百。

translations.literal: In Yongming the emperor ordered that intimates must not casually make recommendations; gentry who lost office were flogged one hundred strokes, commoners likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming the emperor ordered that intimates must not casually make recommendations; gentry who lost office were flogged one hundred strokes, and commoners likewise.

sentences.zh: 上性尊嚴，呂文顯嘗在殿側咳聲高，上使茹法亮訓詰之，以爲不敬，故左右畏威承意，非所隷莫敢有言也。

translations.literal: The emperor was stern by nature; Lü Wenxian once coughed loudly at the emperor's side; the emperor had Ru Faliang reprimand him as disrespectful; therefore those at his side feared his authority and followed his intent, and none outside their jurisdiction dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was severe; when Lü Wenxian once coughed loudly beside the throne, the emperor had Ru Faliang rebuke him for disrespect, so those around him feared his authority, followed his wishes, and none outside their branch dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 時茹法亮掌雜驅使簿，及宣通密敕；

translations.literal: At that time Ru Faliang managed miscellaneous service registers and proclaimed secret edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Ru Faliang then held the miscellaneous service registers and relayed secret edicts;

sentences.zh: 呂文顯掌穀帛事；

translations.literal: Lü Wenxian managed grain and cloth affairs;
translations.idiomatic: while Lü Wenxian managed grain and cloth affairs;

sentences.zh: 其餘舍人無別任。

translations.literal: the other clerks had no separate duties.
translations.idiomatic: the other clerks had no separate duties of their own.

sentences.zh: 虎賁中郎將潘敞掌監功作。

translations.literal: Tiger-Guard Commandant of the Center Pan Chang supervised construction works.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chang of the Tiger Guard Commandant of the Center oversaw construction projects.

sentences.zh: 上使造禪靈寺新成，車駕臨視，甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor had the new Chanling Temple built; the imperial carriage visited and viewed it and was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the new Chanling Temple built; the imperial carriage visited and was very pleased.

sentences.zh: 敞喜，要呂文顯私登寺南門樓，上知之，繫敞上方，而出文顯爲南譙郡，久之乃復。

translations.literal: Chang in delight invited Lü Wenxian privately to climb the temple's southern gate tower; the emperor learned of it, imprisoned Chang in the palace storehouse, and sent Wenxian out as administrator of Southern Qiao; only after long time was he restored.
translations.idiomatic: Chang in delight invited Lü Wenxian privately to climb the temple's southern gate tower; the emperor learned of it, imprisoned Chang in the palace storehouse, and sent Wenxian out as administrator of Southern Qiao; only after a long time was he restored.

sentences.zh: 濟陽江瞿曇、吳興沈徽孚等，以士流舍人通事而已，無權利。

translations.literal: Jiang Qutan of Jiyang, Shen Huifu of Wuxing, and others were gentry clerks for communication alone, without power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Jiang Qutan of Jiyang and Shen Huifu of Wuxing were gentry clerks for communication only, without power or profit.

sentences.zh: 徽孚粗有筆札。

translations.literal: Huifu had some skill with the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Huifu had modest skill with the brush.

sentences.zh: 建武中文詔，多其辭也。

translations.literal: In Jianwu, literary edicts often used his wording.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu, literary edicts often bore his wording.

sentences.zh: 官至黃門郎。

translations.literal: He reached office as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中世已來，宰御天下，萬機碎密，不關外司。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the middle ages onward, those who held the realm governed affairs minute and numerous that did not pass through outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: From the middle ages onward, those who held the realm governed minute and numerous affairs that did not pass through outer offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書八座五曹，各有恒任，係以九卿六府，事存副職。

translations.literal: The eight seats and five bureaus of the Secretariat each had fixed duties, joined with the nine ministers and six offices, with deputy posts for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's eight seats and five bureaus each had standing duties, together with the nine ministers and six offices, where deputy posts carried the work.

sentences.zh: 咸皆冠冕搢紳，任疏人貴，伏奏之務旣寢，趨走之勞亦息。

translations.literal: All were crowned gentry and silk-clad nobles; their duties were remote and their persons exalted; the business of memorials to the throne had already ceased, and the labor of running about had also ended.
translations.idiomatic: All were crowned gentry and silk-clad nobles; their duties were remote and their persons exalted; memorials to the throne had already ceased, and the labor of running about had also ended.

sentences.zh: 關宣所寄，屬當有歸，通驛內外，切自音旨。

translations.literal: What was entrusted for communication and proclamation had to have a place to rest; couriers within and without carried the ruler's very tone.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever was entrusted for proclamation had to land somewhere; couriers inside and outside the palace carried the ruler's own voice.

sentences.zh: 若夫環纓斂笏，俯仰晨昏，贍幄座而竦躬，陪蘭檻而高眄，探求恩色，習睹威顏，遷蘭變鮑，久而彌信，因城社之固，執開壅之機。

translations.literal: As for those with ring and tassel who gathered their tablets, bowing morning and evening, feeding the imperial seat and straightening their bodies, attending by the orchid balustrade and looking down from on high, probing for signs of favor, accustomed to the august countenance—orchid stored long turns to abalone, and over time trust deepens; relying on the solidity of city wall and altar, they hold the mechanism that opens and closes the barrier.
translations.idiomatic: As for those with ring and tassel who gathered their tablets, bowing morning and evening, attending the imperial seat and straightening their bodies, standing by the orchid balustrade and looking down from on high, probing for signs of favor, accustomed to the august countenance—stored with orchid long enough one smells of abalone, and over time trust deepens; relying on the solidity of wall and altar, they hold the mechanism that opens and closes the barrier.

sentences.zh: 長主君世，振裘持領，賞罰事殷，能不踰漏，宮省咳唾，義必先知。

translations.literal: When the ruler was long on the throne, they shook the fur robe and held the collar; rewards and punishments were numerous, yet nothing leaked past them; a cough or spit in the palace—they were sure to know first.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler was long on the throne, they shook the fur robe and held the collar; rewards and punishments were numerous, yet nothing leaked past them—a cough or spit in the palace, they were sure to know first.

sentences.zh: 故能窺盈縮於望景，獲驪珠於龍睡。

translations.literal: Therefore they could spy expansion and contraction from a glance at the sun's shadow and obtain the black pearl while the dragon slept.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they could read expansion and contraction from a glance at the sun's shadow and seize the black pearl while the dragon slept.

sentences.zh: 坐歸聲勢，卧震都鄙。

translations.literal: Sitting, they gathered sonic power; lying down, they shook the capital and its outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, they gathered sonic power; reclining, they shook the capital and its outskirts.

sentences.zh: 賄賂日積，苞苴歲通，富擬公侯，威行州郡。

translations.literal: Bribes piled day by day, gifts passed year by year; their wealth rivaled marquises and dukes, their authority ran through provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes piled day by day, gifts passed year by year; their wealth rivaled marquises and dukes, and their authority ran through provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 制局小司，專典兵力，雲陛天居，亙設蘭錡，羽林精卒，重屯廣衞。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Arms was a petty office that exclusively held military strength; cloud stairs and heaven's dwelling were set with orchid halberds throughout; elite Feathered Forest troops heavily garrisoned the broad guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Arms was a petty office that held military strength; cloud stairs and heaven's dwelling were lined with orchid halberds; elite Feathered Forest troops heavily garrisoned the broad guard.

sentences.zh: 至于元戎啓轍，式候還麾，遮迾清道，神行案轡，督察來往，馳騖輦轂，驅役分部，親承几案，領護所攝，示總成規。

translations.literal: As for the grand army setting out and returning with banners, screening the clear road, divine speed with reins on the writing table, inspecting comings and goings, galloping at the chariot hub, driving and assigning sections, personally receiving the writing desk, leading and protecting what they oversaw, showing the overall rule.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand army set out and returned with banners, screening the clear road, reins on the writing table at divine speed, they inspected comings and goings, galloped at the chariot hub, drove and assigned sections, personally received the writing desk, led what they oversaw, and showed the overall rule.

sentences.zh: 若徵兵動衆，大興民役，行留之儀，請託在手，斷割牢稟，賣弄文符，捕叛追亡，長戍遠謪，軍有千齡之壽，室無百年之鬼，害政傷民，於此爲蠹。

translations.literal: If troops were levied and masses mobilized, great labor conscripted, rules of movement and stay—all entreaties were in their hands; they carved prison provisions and trafficked in documents; capturing rebels and pursuing fugitives, long garrison and distant exile; armies had men who lived a thousand years, households without ghosts of a hundred years—harm to government and injury to the people: here was the vermin.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were levied and masses mobilized, with great labor conscripted, rules of movement and stay—all entreaties were in their hands; they carved prison provisions and trafficked in documents; capturing rebels and pursuing fugitives, long garrison and distant exile—armies had men who lived a thousand years, households without ghosts of a hundred years: here government was harmed and the people injured.

sentences.zh: 況乎主幼時昏，其爲讒慝，亦何可勝紀也！

translations.literal: How much more when the ruler was young and the times benighted—their slander and wickedness, how could it all be recorded!
translations.idiomatic: All the more when the throne was young and the age benighted—how could their slander and villainy even be counted!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：恩澤而侯，親倖爲舊。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Favored with grace and enfeoffed as lords, intimate favorites of old.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Favored with grace and enfeoffed as lords, they were intimate favorites of old.

sentences.zh: 便煩左右，旣貴且富。

translations.literal: They took on troubles at the ruler's side, becoming both exalted and rich.
translations.idiomatic: They took on troubles at the ruler's side and became both exalted and rich.

translations.literal: Note 1.
translations.idiomatic: See note 1.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
